authors: Caves EM, Fernandez-Juricic E, Kelley LA
title: Ecological and morphological correlates of visual acuity in birds: supplementary Tables S1 and S2 (acuity, eye size and body mass for 94 species)
why: Would give a species-level acuity for every bird in the 94-species table (corvids, a sandpiper, flycatchers, falcons, owls, ducks) in one file; the article text is open and names no per-species values for the common backyard species.
get: open-access supplement on the journal page (cc-by); Table S1 download

title: Complex distribution of avian color vision systems revealed by sequencing the SWS1 opsin from total DNA
why: Sequences for crows, jays, raptors, gulls and others; says which common families are violet type and which ultraviolet type (the 2013 and 2011 papers I opened cite it for Corvidae, Laridae and Falconiformes).

authors: Odeen A, Hastad O, Alstrom P
title: Evolution of ultraviolet vision in the largest avian radiation - the passerines: Additional files 1 to 3 (species list with site-90 residue)
why: Additional file 1 lists the opsin residue for 56 passerine species including the Northern crested caracara; the article text I read gives families but the species list is in the file.
get: open-access additional files on the journal page

title: The phylogenetic distribution of ultraviolet sensitivity in birds: Additional file 2 (every species with its violet or ultraviolet type)
why: Supplementary table for the whole of Aves; Table 1 in the article lists only the 40 new species.
get: open-access additional files on the journal page

title: Head-bobs in birds: the eyes have it
why: Commentary on what head-bobbing does for vision; would settle which of the wader view's walkers bob, and whether chickens and pigeons hold the head for the same length of time.

title: Visual fields in herons (Ardeidae): panoramic vision beneath the bill
why: Gives the visual field of herons, the commonest wader species in the app; the wader view has no field value of its own.

title: Visual fields in the Black-crowned Night Heron Nycticorax nycticorax: nocturnality does not result in owl-like features
why: Field and binocular overlap in a heron, to compare with the daytime herons.

title: Near-field visual acuity in Japanese jungle crows (Corvus macrorhynchos)
why: The only crow acuity in the collection; crows and jays are among the commonest birds met and have no measured sharpness in the log.

title: The visual acuity and refractive state of the American kestrel (Falco sparverius)
why: Behavioural acuity of the commonest small falcon in Florida (the round 1 list had it too).

authors: Porter ML, Kingston ACN, McCrea AE, Ryan DG, Lal KK, Hart NS, Cronin TW
title: Characterization of visual pigments, oil droplets, lens and cornea in the whooping crane Grus americana
why: Only measured crane; would let the sandhill crane borrow pigments and the ultraviolet question inside the genus.

authors: Guillemain M, Martin GR, Fritz H
title: Feeding methods, visual fields and vigilance in dabbling ducks (Anatidae)
why: Fields of several ducks at species level (whistling-ducks, teal, Muscovy duck are the commonest in Alachua).

authors: Mitkus M, Potier S, Martin GR, Duriez O, Kelber A
title: Eye size, fovea, and foraging ecology in accipitriform raptors
why: Eye size and fovea across Accipitriformes at species level; would sort kites, harriers and ospreys from buteos.

authors: Inzunza O, Bravo H, Smith RL, Angel M
title: Topography and morphology of retinal ganglion cells in Falconiforms: a study on predatory and carrion-eater birds
why: Ganglion cell maps of predatory and carrion-eating falconiforms, which bears on the caracaras and the vultures.

authors: Fernandez-Juricic E, et al. (chimango caracara acuity)
title: Visual acuity in an opportunistic raptor, the chimango caracara (Milvago chimango)
why: Nearest measured relative of the crested caracara, which Alachua records often.

title: Retinal ganglion cell topography of five species of ground-foraging birds
why: Ganglion cell maps of ground-foraging songbirds and doves, with species acuities.

authors: Lisney TJ, Rubene D, Rozsa J, Lovlie H, Hakansson J, Kelber A
title: Behavioural assessment of flicker fusion frequency in chicken Gallus gallus domesticus
why: Chicken flicker speed, for the wader view's gamebirds.

authors: Potier S, Mitkus M, Kelber A
title: Visual adaptations of diurnal and nocturnal raptors
journal: Seminars in Cell and Developmental Biology
why: Review table of flicker, acuity and fields by species across raptors.

title: Bird colour vision: from cones to perception
why: Review of what is measured behaviourally in which species.

title: The Sensory Ecology of Birds (Oxford University Press): chapters on vision and visual fields
